author: claude-opus-5 (agent; Freelingo p2fix-author-u24-u30 lane)

authority.note: The brief is a derived snapshot and G5 never reads it. It is the authority on WHICH slots exist and WHAT each allows; the enforcer is still the `stale_ledger` axis against the ledger G4 emits in the build being run. If the course is rebuilt at a different ingest cap, every digest below moves and this shard has to be re-keyed — the Spanish does not change, only the 16-hex field and the slot keys.

deliverable.lesson_index_space: G4's GLOBAL lesson index, copied verbatim from the brief. Unit 24 is lessons 137-140, unit 30 is 171-176. The committed 160-row content/es/candidates.jsonl keys its slots per unit and therefore fills nothing; this shard copies its field shape and none of its slot keys.

row_contract.why_not_allowed_lemmas: The task brief named `allowed_lemmas` as a required key. The ledger-freeze lane replaces it with `ledger_digest` for the reason units 24-30 make sharpest: the allowed set here is 729-927 lemmas, so restating it on all 20 candidates of every slot is the same list written 2,120 times. `allowed_lemmas_count` rides along as a human cross-check of the same claim.

verification.script: scratchpad/verify_against_brief.py — independent of the assembler: it recomputes each brief digest from the brief's own known_lemmas|new_lemmas with the ledger-freeze formula, re-runs the G1 adapter (es_core_news_md 3.8.0) over every text, and applies REJECT_AXES in order.
verification.repo_suite: pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test — 114 files, 1316 tests, all passing, EXIT=0. This lane changes no TypeScript; the run is a guard against having broken something outside its lane, not evidence about the content.

how_the_slot_set_was_found_before_the_br: The brief did not exist when authoring started, so the gap list was reproduced locally with `coursekit build es --only g0..g4 --set max_pairs=200000` — the same cap pack-ci.yml uses. That run gave 920 gap slots course-wide and 221 in units 24-30 (14/47/29/35/35/26/35), matching the 281b623 CI measurement per unit. The frozen brief has 490 and 106, because the ledger-freeze patch also records a reserved gap's lemma as `shown`, which frees the corpus to fill the slots that used to gap. The 106 lemmas the brief reserves are EXACTLY the 106 this lane had already written pools for — zero missing, zero unused — because the reservation rule (`pending[:MAX_NEW_LEMMAS_PER_EXERCISE]`, head of the unit's not-yet-shown target lemmas) was derived from the same code. The 115 practice slots the unpatched run produced are not in the frozen course and are not shipped.

backtranslation_scoring.judged_by: agent — the same agent wrote the Spanish and scored the round trip, which the rubric's own 'Honest limits' section calls a floor on quality rather than a measurement of it
backtranslation_scoring.why_not_uniform_fours: 23.3% are 3s. A 3 is recorded wherever the English a learner is shown differs from a literal round trip in a way that is about English rather than about meaning: `de` rendered as a possessive ('the boss's toast' for `el brindis del jefe`), `mucho` before a mass noun, `hacer ciclismo` as 'to cycle', `superior`/`inferior` as 'upper'/'lower', `mirar` as 'to examine' in the clinic sentences, `ración` as 'portion'. One row scored 2 during authoring (`El médico busca el dolor de cabeza.` — 'busca' is not 'looks into') was replaced rather than shipped, and the verifier confirms no row below 3 is in the file.

known_limits: One judge, no blind pass: the scores are this lane's own judgement of its own Spanish. The paid native-speaker sample at the end of P2 is the measurement; these 2,120 rows are 23% of the course's authored content and will be over-represented in a stratified 300-item draw, so a systematic error here is expensive.

The vocabulary ceiling is the curriculum's lexeme list, not natural Spanish. `es_core_news_md` lemmatises several common forms outside that list, so some phrasings a native would reach for first are unavailable: `buena`/`buenos` lemmatise to `buen` (only masculine singular `bueno` is in the ledger), `gracias` to `gracia`, conjugated `comer` to `come`/`como`. Sentences were written around those rather than through them, which flattens a handful of them.

Practice-only slots do not exist in the frozen course, so every row here introduces exactly one new lemma. If a later rebuild reintroduces empty-`new_lemmas` slots, this lane's review-sentence pool (about 400 validated sentences) is in the run's scratchpad and can be re-keyed.
notes_for_the_next_author: es_core_news_md lemma traps confirmed against the real ledger: `buena`/`buenos` -> `buen`, `gracias` -> `gracia`, `mala` -> `malo`, `enferma` -> `enferma`, adjectival `derecha`/`izquierda` -> `derecho`/`izquierdo`, `euros` -> `euros`, `cuántas` -> `cuántos`, and `felicita`, `patina`, `salta`, `apuntes` -> `apunt`. Use the infinitive for `felicitar` and `patinar`.
A sentence-initial conjugated verb is frequently mis-lemmatised after capitalisation (`Llego`, `Busco`, `Guardo`, `Bebo`, `Vas`, `Quieres`, `Estudias`). Lead with a subject or a determiner.

NOT in the units 1-23 ledger, despite feeling basic: `ahora`, `desde`, `así`, `malo`, `mejor` (until unit 27 introduces it), `problema`, `normal`, `importante`, `tiempo`, `parte`, `cuerpo`, `ver`, `nosotros`, `ella`, `ellos`. IN the ledger: `que`, `a`, `al`, `del`.
Token count is spaCy's and includes punctuation: `¿` and `?` are one token each, so a five-word question is seven tokens. Every row here lands in 4-10.
